$comment: Canonical game feature tree shown on the status page's Features tab (https://bjor2.github.io/steampunk-miner/status/#features). Edit by hand; how-to in docs/features/README.md. status: built | partial | planned. issues: GitHub issue numbers. planet: campaign planet it unlocks on. group: a heading node without its own status.
title: Steampunk Miner
description: Infinite 2D steampunk mining game in the spirit of Motherload: drill into round planets, haul ore home, sell, upgrade, harvest the core and travel on through a 40-planet campaign toward endless play.

areas.title: Vehicle & Movement
areas.description: The mining rig itself: how it drives, climbs, drills and survives on a round world.

children.title: Driving on a round world
children.description: Drive left and right along the curved surface and tunnels; controls follow the rig, so 'down' always points toward the core.

children.title: Thruster climb (lift)
children.description: Hold W to fire the steam thruster and climb against gravity; it also swings the drill to face up. Thrust drains energy fastest.

children.title: Radial gravity
children.description: Gravity always pulls toward the planet centre and weakens near it, so climbing out of a deep shaft is the real cost of a dive.

children.title: Swivelling drill head
children.description: The drill turns between four directions (left, right, down, up) without turning the body, so you can tunnel any way you like.

children.title: Energy
children.description: One shared energy tank powers everything; it is your clock on every trip.

children.title: Energy tank
children.description: Driving, drilling, thrusting and gun shots all draw from a single boiler tank that you recharge at the platform.

children.title: Action energy costs
children.description: Each action drains at its own rate: thrust most, then drilling, then driving; boring upward costs about 2.5x more than boring down.

children.title: Low-energy warnings
children.description: Warnings at 25% and 10% that also account for the energy needed to climb home from your current depth, so they never lie about the way back.

children.title: Stranding & rescue tow
children.description: Run dry away from the pad and the rig strands; press R (or wait a few seconds) and the tow drags you home for a small fee, losing the ore in the hold. No game over.

children.title: Safe pad
children.description: Running out of energy on the dock pad never strands you; you can always dock.

children.title: Hull & Cargo
children.description: How much punishment the rig takes and how much it can carry.

children.title: Hull health
children.description: Hull soaks hits from enemies, cave-ins, heat, lava and your own blasts; repair it at the platform.

children.title: Wreck & tow
children.description: At zero hull the rig is wrecked and towed back to the dock: hull refilled, cargo ore lost, core fragments still banked.

children.title: Cargo capacity
children.description: Ore fills a limited hold; once it is full, newly mined ore is lost, so you have to head home and sell.

children.title: Look & Feel
children.description: How the rig shows what it is doing and how far it has grown.

children.title: Animated machinery
children.description: Wheels roll with speed, the drill spins as it bites, pistons pump with thrust, the boiler breathes and landings squash the chassis.

children.title: Headlamp
children.description: A lamp follows the drill's facing and lights the rock you are about to cut.

children.title: Three visual tiers
children.description: The rig visibly grows: tier 2 adds side armour and a second stack, tier 3 a bore-collar drill, a second boiler and a second lamp, as your total upgrade levels rise.

children.title: Mounted modules on the rig
children.description: Bought modules show on the vehicle: the gun turret swings its barrel toward targets and the charge rack sits on the hull.

children.title: Planned vehicle modules
children.description: Campaign additions scheduled in the locked unlock schedule but not built yet.

children.title: Cargo wagon
children.description: Hitch a wagon behind the rig for more storage; later wagon types and a second slot live on this beat.

children.title: Side drill arms
children.description: Side cutters on the drill's flank: switched on with F, they cut one cell beside the bit at the bit's own power, hardness and energy, so the bore is wider but no faster. Built as a drill-gear tech node; the store buy and its model on the miner come later.

children.title: Steam shield
children.description: A steam curtain that turns aside enemy hits and collapse crush for a short window (at most half of each hit); it never stops heat or lava. Built as the mobility lane's power-up and bought at the Upgrade bay once researched; its curtain on the rig comes later.

children.title: Grav anchor
children.description: A toggle that pins the miner to the wall or ceiling it touches, so it can drill while anchored; it draws 1% of the tank a second and drops off at an empty tank. Bought at the Upgrade bay once researched; its model on the rig comes later.

children.title: Buoyancy tanks
children.description: A toggle that hovers the miner in open cavern air without thrust, drawing 1.5% of the tank a second. Bought at the Upgrade bay once researched; its model on the rig comes later.

children.title: Escape thrusters
children.description: A one-shot cartridge that kicks the miner up the shaft in one long burst, stopping at the first solid cell. The store buy and its puff and thump come later.

areas.title: Drilling & Terrain
areas.description: Cutting through the ground, keeping tunnels standing, and blasting when the drill is not enough.

children.title: Smooth carved ground
children.description: The ground is a fluid density field: the drill carves round tunnels at any angle instead of chopping square blocks, so sideways digging feels natural.

children.title: Hardness vs drill
children.description: Each rock's hardness against your drill sets the dig time, up to 2.5 tiles a second; deeper bands and later planets are harder.

children.title: 'Needs a better tip'
children.description: If your drill tip is under a quarter of the rock's hardness the drill only skids: no progress, no energy spent, a clear sign to upgrade.

children.title: Upward and sideways boring
children.description: Dig up, down or sideways; boring upward combines thrust and drill and costs the most energy.

children.title: Drill-tip breakpoints
children.description: Retune so each planet's tip upgrades visibly cut dig time (to 0.7x or less by departure). In progress.

children.title: Casing & Lining
children.description: The rig lines its own tunnels with cement as it drills.

children.title: Automatic casing
children.description: While drilling, the rig lays a cement lining ring about every half metre behind it, with no button to press.

children.title: Casing grade
children.description: Lining strength; each depth band needs a grade at least its number (the core needs 5). Buy higher grades at the Upgrade bay.

children.title: Lining bill
children.description: Lining fresh rock costs a little per metre; the bill is paid out of your next payout at the Sell bay, and whatever that visit can't cover is forgiven. Never debt.

children.title: Re-drilling your casing
children.description: You can drill back through your own lining; lined walls still pay their ore, and the drill sings a higher note in casing.

children.title: Refractory lining
children.description: A firebrick lining type for heat planets, bought once at the Upgrade bay: it keeps lava out and cools the rig faster, at 1.5x the lining cost.

children.title: Insulated lining
children.description: Lining type for frozen planets.

children.title: Grounded lining
children.description: Lining type for magnetic and electrified planets.

children.title: Cave-ins
children.description: Tunnels lined too weakly for their depth can collapse around you.

children.title: Weak-tunnel collapse
children.description: A tunnel stretch whose lining grade is too low for its band caves in when your rig is within 16 m; unlined rock never does.

children.title: Collapse warning
children.description: About a second of growing cracks, falling dust and a rising rumble before the walls refill.

children.title: Crush damage
children.description: A rig caught in the refill loses hull and is left in a pocket of air; a wreck goes to the tow.

children.title: Blasting charges
children.description: A tool for hard rock, shafts and enemies in the way, unlocked on planet 7.

children.title: Plant a charge
children.description: Press B to stick a charge on the wall the drill faces; it blows after a two-second fuse.

children.title: Blast trade-off
children.description: Clears a 2.5-tile radius instantly but only about 40% of the ore survives; core and rock harder than the deep band resist, and lined rings hold.

children.title: Blast damage
children.description: The blast hurts you if you stand too close and heavily damages enemies in range; it can also set off weak tunnels.

children.title: Charge rack
children.description: Buy charges and extra rack slots (3 up to 8) at the Upgrade bay.

children.title: Fuse warning & scorch
children.description: The HUD warns of a live fuse nearby; the charge blinks on the wall and leaves a scorch mark.

children.title: Dynamite sizes
children.description: Ten charge sizes from a 2.5- to a 24-tile blast, one more every 3 planets from planet 10, each taking more rack slots and costing more; V picks the size B plants. Sizes 7 to 10 wait for the plunger, and their own looks and rack panel are still to come.

areas.title: Planets & World
areas.description: Round, fully drillable planets, their layers, their cores and the journey between them.

children.title: Round, fully drillable planets
children.description: Every planet is a disc you can dig into from anywhere on its surface, down to the core and beyond.

children.title: Depth bands
children.description: Five bands from crust to deep rock, each harder, richer and more dangerous, then the core.

children.title: Caves
children.description: Natural caverns open from band 2 downward and give crawlers somewhere to live.

children.title: Growing planets
children.description: Each planet is larger than the last, from 300 m radius toward 1000 m.

children.title: Seeded worlds
children.description: Each planet comes from a world seed, so the same seed always builds the same world.

children.title: Guaranteed early ore
children.description: The first dives always pay something.

children.title: Starter vein
children.description: Planet 1 places an easy vein within 15 m of the dock, in a zone no enemy spawns in.

children.title: Dock ore guarantee
children.description: If no ore lies under the dock, one shallow patch is placed straight below it.

children.title: Planet types
children.description: Planet archetypes change gravity, palette, resources and hazards.

children.title: Base planet
children.description: Planet 1: standard gravity, metal-rich ground and its own palette.

children.title: Heavy planet
children.description: Planet 2 on: gravity 1.25x, crystal-rich ground and a new palette.

children.title: Heat / lava planets
children.description: Planets 8 to 16 (the Fire act): a heat gauge, lava pockets and a firebrick palette, announced by a stinger.

children.title: Frozen planets
children.description: A cold planet family.

children.title: Magnetic / electrified planets
children.description: Planets that interfere with the rig's systems.

children.title: Hollow planets
children.description: Planets with open interiors to cross.

children.title: Unstable cores
children.description: Harvesting the core starts an escape run.

children.title: Planet core
children.description: The core is the major objective of every planet.

children.title: Core region
children.description: A disc of very hard core tiles at the planet centre.

children.title: Core fragments
children.description: Each core tile drops a fragment; fragments are never sold, they pay for travel.

children.title: Core bay
children.description: Fragments bank at the platform whenever you dock or get towed, so core is never lost.

children.title: Core reached & completed
children.description: The first core tile brings a Guild transmission and a stinger; filling the quota completes the planet and fits the platform's core drive.

children.title: Planet travel
children.description: Moving the operation to the next world.

children.title: Travel to the next planet
children.description: From the dock, pay the fee plus the fragment quota (40% of the core's tiles) to move to the next planet; extra fragments stay banked.

children.title: Travel transition
children.description: A short travel card of up to 10 seconds that you can skip.

children.title: Fresh world on arrival
children.description: The new planet starts untouched; your rig, levels, cargo and artefact come with you.

children.title: No travel cap
children.description: Planets keep coming by formula past the authored campaign; nothing stops travel.

areas.title: Resources & Ore
areas.description: What you dig up and what it is worth.

children.title: Endless ore tiers
children.description: Every band and planet steps up the ore tier; each tier is worth 1.5x the last, with no top.

children.title: Ore families
children.description: Metal and crystal families with their own shapes; each planet weights them differently.

children.title: Ore catalogue and deeper previews
children.description: Every ore is a family at a tier with a graded name, such as Raw Brassvein or Crystal Quartzine, from a twelve-family catalogue. A few patches in each band hold ore one or two tiers deeper, worth and as hard as that deeper ore, and more of them the deeper the band. Planets still grow only metal and crystal until the per-planet ore mix lands.

children.title: Ore patches
children.description: Ore sits in larger, rarer patches (bigger deeper down) that you find by exposing them.

children.title: Tier glow
children.description: Higher tiers glow brighter and sparkle more; tiers stay readable even in greyscale.

children.title: Ore looks that escalate with depth
children.description: Twelve ore families with their own silhouettes, each climbing five visual grades as the tier deepens: plain form, then sheen, crystal structure, inner light and finally its own effect with arcs, authored and baked in Blender and shipped as three 4096 px atlases. Not drawn in the game yet: the atlas renderer, the twelve-family cells and the neighbour light are kernel follow-ups.

children.title: Ore pickup
children.description: A cell's ore drops into the hold once you've carved through most of it, lined or not.

children.title: Refined ore
children.description: Ore refined at the Refinery bay sells for 25% more than raw.

children.title: More resource families
children.description: Each planet from planet 3 mines its own mix of twelve ore families, set by its act (Foothold, Fire, Frost, Lodestone, Hollow, then cycling in endless) and its seed, with one signature ore in the two deepest bands that sells a tier up and needs a better drill tip. Still to come: each family's own look in the ground and the extractors that free the gated ores.

children.title: Mining gates
children.description: From planet 7 the rarer ore cells are locked: some need a better drill tip, some an extractor, some a charge of dynamite. Common ore is never locked, and no lock holds back more than 15% of a band's ore value. Still to come: the lock markers, sounds and hint chip (#238) and each extractor's own verb (#237).

children.title: Dense ore
children.description: Rare previews of drill-class ores, and rare previews whose extractor has not arrived yet, are dense: the drill only skids until your last full drill-tip level is one past the ore's tier.

children.title: Sealed ore shells
children.description: Amberbone and Obsidian rare previews sit in shells the drill cannot open; a charge of the size the shell asks for frees the whole cell, full ore and no blast loss.

children.title: Signature ores that need a better drill
children.description: On planets 3 to 6 the signature ore is five tiers harder and the drill only scratches it until your tip catches up.

children.title: Extractors
children.description: Five extractors, the Resonance Fork, Containment Hood, Acid Etcher, Induction Coil and Aether Tether, each open one class of rare ore and the planet's signature, arriving on planets 5, 12, 19, 26 and 33. Without one the drill skids off, or the ore vents or floats away. The Upgrade bay sells each from its own planet once its tech node is researched; still to come: those nodes and the extractors' own verbs (tune, capture, mark, pull, tow).

areas.title: Economy, Platform & Docks
areas.description: The mobile platform on the surface: bays, services and prices.

children.title: Mobile platform
children.description: Your base stands on a pad at the surface of every planet and moves with you.

children.title: Docking
children.description: Stop on a bay's pad and press Space or E to dock; the bay's screen slides in.

children.title: Sell bay
children.description: Copper-and-amber bay for turning ore into money.

children.title: Sell ore
children.description: Sell one tier or the whole hold at the current unit prices.

children.title: Recharge
children.description: Refill the energy tank for a small charge.

children.title: Sell, repair & recharge
children.description: One key (Q) sells everything, repairs and recharges at the exact total shown.

children.title: Collect refined batches
children.description: Ready refinery batches are paid in here, 25% richer than raw ore.

children.title: Lining bill on screen
children.description: Shows the visit's lining bill, what it paid and what leaving will forgive.

children.title: Sell burst
children.description: Selling throws the ore up into the Exchange and bursts coins out of its stack that fly to the money counter, which rolls as they land; a big sale lights a gold flare, and a paid lining bill peels coins off to a 'Lining −X' tag. Flat stand-in shapes and synthesised sounds until the final sprite sheets.

children.title: Upgrade bay
children.description: Steel-and-teal bay where the rig gets stronger.

children.title: Buy upgrades
children.description: The six vehicle tracks, each a plaque with icon, level, rivet pips toward the next big level, next cost and 'before to after' stats.

children.title: Extra rows
children.description: Casing grade, lining type, guns and charges rows appear as each is unlocked.

children.title: Repair
children.description: Repair the hull for a price that scales with the damage.

children.title: Workshop showcase
children.description: The rig stands on the Works' turntable in the main view with nothing over it, and the six tracks are plaques around it with leader lines to their parts: selecting one lights its part and turns the turntable, and every purchase sways that part, wider for a big level-up. Still missing: the milestone parts and cards (#228), the coins pulled into the part, the camera punch-in and the final art.

children.title: Hold-to-buy chains
children.description: Hold Buy (a long-press on touch, once the plaque's card is open) to buy the same upgrade faster and faster: a click buys one, then a short wind-up, then quicker steps up to 10 a second, a breath at each big level-up, and a stop on release, sliding off, can't afford or the service reserve, each with its own cadence. Plaques tempt with 'can buy ×12, 1 big level' and count the running chain; each plaque is its track's item card, opened by a tap or menu focus.

children.title: Escalating purchase sound
children.description: Each purchase ticks a ratchet that climbs a pentatonic scale and layers up as the chain speeds, a whistle-and-clang for a big level-up, and a cadence when the chain stops, capped at 4 ratchet voices and 1 flourish. Synthesised stand-in tones until the final sounds.

children.title: Upgrade icons
children.description: One icon language across the bay: a riveted plate for each track and module, a padlock or star badge for locked and maxed rows, a rim glint when a buy is open, and only the price turns red when money is short.

children.title: Install animation
children.description: A bought part bolts on with a puff of steam (instant with reduced motion).

children.title: Workshop milestones
children.description: A few big level-ups per track bring a new behaviour and a visible part on the miner: the first two majors of every track swap in or move its tier parts. The list is data; each behaviour (bit-spin flourish, piston pump, hopper tip, part swap) is built by its own ticket.

children.title: Refinery bay
children.description: Ember-and-brass third bay that bolts onto the pad from planet 3.

children.title: Refinery unlock
children.description: The bay appears on arrival at planet 3, with its own look, stack smoke and a reveal stinger.

children.title: Refine batches
children.description: Load up to half your hold of one ore tier into a slot; it refines over 3 minutes, even while you dive or travel.

children.title: Refinery slots
children.description: Start with one slot and buy up to three.

children.title: Mobile refining
children.description: A later mode that refines on the move, folded into this bay.

children.title: Bay screens
children.description: Shared steampunk frame with a brass shutter, one accent colour per bay, large readable text and full keyboard control.

children.title: Right bay for each job
children.description: Each service belongs to one bay; at the other bay it shows as a disabled sign that points you along the pad.

children.title: Item cards
children.description: Every shop entry, platform card and service tooltip shows a one-line flavour text and live stats: now, next, the change and its share, and the cap still to gain. Tap opens a card and a second tap buys; hover, focus or a touch hold shows a tooltip.

children.title: Platform grows
children.description: The outpost hub gains a glowing core drive with a fill gauge when the core quota is met, then the Refinery bay from planet 3.

children.title: Prices
children.description: Prices climb on formulas so the economy can run forever.

children.title: Ore prices
children.description: Every ore tier has a unit price that grows by a fixed ratio per tier.

children.title: Exponential upgrade prices
children.description: Each upgrade level costs more by a fixed ratio; drill prices were flattened to match ore growth.

children.title: Two-tier levels
children.description: Every big level is ten steps: nine pips that each add a little, then the big level-up with the rest. The ten steps cost what the level did, so a good trip buys many in a row; the guns level the same way.

children.title: Rescue fee
children.description: The tow costs a small share of your money, with a floor and a cap.

children.title: Travel fee
children.description: Travel costs money as well as core fragments, scaled to the planet.

children.title: Planned facilities
children.description: Further platform facilities in the campaign schedule.

children.title: Specialist merchants
children.description: Merchants with their own specialised trades.

children.title: Scanner station
children.description: Reveals what lies underground. From planet 14 its mast stands on the Assay & Exchange and the camera pans to it on first landing; the scanning itself is not built.

children.title: Drone bay
children.description: Hauler drones that ferry cargo. From planet 20 its hangar stands on the Works' roof and the camera pans to it on first landing; the drones are not built.

children.title: Research lab
children.description: Research to unlock new technology. From planet 15 its annex stands behind the Works and the camera pans to it on first landing; the lab's research is not built.

children.title: Quest office
children.description: NPC contracts with their own rewards.

children.title: Core forge
children.description: A late facility that turns core material into special upgrades.

areas.title: Upgrades & Progression
areas.description: Vertical upgrades that scale forever and the campaign schedule of new things to do.

children.title: Vehicle upgrade tracks
children.description: Six uncapped tracks bought at the Upgrade bay.

children.title: Drill power
children.description: Digs faster through any rock.

children.title: Drill tip
children.description: Lets the drill bite harder rock; the gate to deeper bands and planets.

children.title: Engine
children.description: Raises top speed, acceleration and climbing power, with gradually smaller gains.

children.title: Boiler
children.description: Adds energy capacity for longer dives.

children.title: Cargo hold
children.description: Adds room for four more ore per level.

children.title: Hull
children.description: Adds 12% hull per level.

children.title: Uncapped levels
children.description: Every track goes on forever while its price climbs exponentially, so progress never hits a wall.

children.title: Module upgrades
children.description: Casing grades, gun levels, charge-rack slots and refinery slots are bought alongside the tracks.

children.title: Campaign unlock schedule
children.description: A locked 40-planet plan: every planet brings something new.

children.title: 40-planet schedule
children.description: A data-driven schedule of new enemies, facilities, upgrades and planet types for each campaign planet.

children.title: Unlock on arrival
children.description: Features unlock when you reach their planet, announced by stingers.

children.title: Slice beats (planets 1-2)
children.description: Sell and upgrade loop, platform, crawler, burrower, core harvest and the second planet.

children.title: Planet 3: Refinery bay
children.description: The first new facility.

children.title: Planet 4: Automated guns
children.description: The first weapon.

children.title: Planet 6: Tunnel wrecker
children.description: A new enemy family that goes after your tunnels.

children.title: Planet 7: Blasting charges
children.description: A new mining tool.

children.title: Planet 8: Heat & refractory lining
children.description: The first new planet type and its counter-upgrade.

children.title: Pacing target
children.description: Aim of 45-60 minutes per planet; the target is set, but a stall on planet 9 is being diagnosed.

children.title: Felt-progression gate
children.description: A regression check that keeps upgrades feeling meaningful across the campaign.

children.title: End-of-slice card
children.description: Completing planet 2's core shows an end-of-slice card; play continues behind it.

children.title: Endless mode
children.description: Unlocks after the finale at planet 40, so progression goes on past the campaign.

children.title: Powerups
children.description: Up to five power-up slots, used with keys 1 to 5 or the touch slot column; charges refill free with the dock recharge, and three cradles open slots 3 to 5. The slots, charges, the mobility and sensing lanes and buying researched one-offs and cradles at the Upgrade bay are built; the other lanes and buying consumables by the unit come with their tickets.

children.title: Mobility and survival power-ups
children.description: Grapple winch (reel up to a wall or ceiling, refused at no cost with nothing to hook), emergency ballast, heat sink flask (once you own refractory lining), steam boost, rivet patch kit (hold still to plate the hull; moving gives the kit back), steam shield, smoke canister, grav anchor, buoyancy tanks and escape thruster, each with its tech node, Marks and item card. The five one-offs are bought at the Upgrade bay once researched; buying the consumables by the unit, and the models and effects on the rig, come later.

children.title: Sensing power-ups
children.description: Echo sounder (a ping marks caves, lava, ore silhouettes and gate badges round the miner for a while), threat periscope (an arrow for every enemy in range, with its family, distance band and burrower dust), assay lens (cards over the ore in sight: family, grade, lead, sell price, gate), hazard barometer (warns of lava or weak lining a few cells ahead), survey flare mortar (maps a ring where it lands until the dock) and signal buoy (a pin every miner in the world sees, re-pinging its ring as vehicles pass), each with its tech node, Marks and item card. What they reveal is drawn on each client and never changes the world. The echo and the passives are bought at the Upgrade bay once researched; the galvanic probe and void sounder wait for magnetic and hollow planets, and codex contact from scans for #243.

children.title: Tech tree
children.description: Research nodes with money to unlock store items: five lanes on a planet ruler, Marks every 3 planets that step an item's charges, cooldown and effect in play, endless combos from P41, a tree screen from the HUD. The rules and screen are built, and the mobility, sensing and drill-gear lanes are in; the other lanes show 'coming soon' until their slices register nodes.

children.title: Drill gear
children.description: Vibratory bit (soft ground ahead crumbles), spoil auger (fills the tunnel behind you, C to switch), side cutters, thaw crown, sampling corer (C: draws a plug from the first ore ahead, refused at no cost by a gated or core cell) and reach boom, each in its drill socket with its tech node, Marks and item card, sold at the Upgrade bay once researched. The twin-bit head and dielectric bit wait for the mechanics they answer. Their models on the miner come later.

children.title: Gear on the rig and power-up effects
children.description: Every bought extractor, drill head, collar and flank gear, scanner horn, winch, periscope and crate shows on the miner at its own mount, and each power-up cradle wears a brass Mark plate, gilded once Mastered. Power-ups draw their effect: brine lines, tumbling nodules, sounder rings, steam. Owned items of registered lanes (mobility and sensing today) show on the rig; extractors stay folded until they unfold on a matching ore (#237), and each plate shows the Mark its item acts at (#249).

areas.title: Hazards, Enemies & Combat
areas.description: Combat grows out of mining: the drill is your first weapon.

children.title: Drill-contact combat
children.description: Facing matters: point the drill at trouble.

children.title: The drill always hurts
children.description: Enemies that touch the drill's nose are pinned and drilled every moment they stay there.

children.title: Three hit zones
children.description: Hits from the front cost a quarter, from the side full damage, from behind double, so you turn to face attackers.

children.title: Telegraphed attacks
children.description: Enemies wind up visibly before they lunge, giving you time to turn the drill.

children.title: Safe at the dock
children.description: Docking ends the trip: hunting enemies leave you alone.

children.title: Enemies
children.description: The roster grows over the campaign.

children.title: Crawler
children.description: A cave-dwelling hunter from planet 1 that stalks and lunges at the rig.

children.title: Burrower
children.description: Swims through solid rock from planet 2 and gives itself away with a tremor before it strikes.

children.title: Tunnel wrecker
children.description: From planet 6, gnaws your lined route home so it caves in; it flees from the rig and can only be caught when cornered. A scrape warns you.

children.title: Magma tick
children.description: A heat-planet pest.

children.title: Core guardian
children.description: A guardian in the core chamber.

children.title: Frost spitter
children.description: A ranged frozen-planet enemy.

children.title: Swarm nests
children.description: Nests that release swarms.

children.title: Ore thief
children.description: Steals ore from your hold.

children.title: EMP mite
children.description: Disables the rig's equipment.

children.title: Enemy scaling
children.description: Enemies get tougher every planet and band; the crust stays free of them and the middle bands are busiest.

children.title: Automated guns
children.description: A hull turret from planet 4 that covers your flanks.

children.title: Mount the turret
children.description: Bolt guns onto the rig at the Upgrade bay, then level them up.

children.title: Auto targeting
children.description: The turret shoots enemies at your sides and rear within range; the front is left to the drill.

children.title: Steam-powered shots
children.description: Each shot costs energy, and the guns go quiet before they could strand you (low-steam badge).

children.title: Auto / Off toggle
children.description: Press G to switch the guns between Auto and Off.

children.title: Deployable defences
children.description: A later mode for placeable defences, folded into the guns.

children.title: Heat & lava
children.description: The hazards of the Fire act (planets 8-16).

children.title: Heat gauge
children.description: Heat builds with depth and drilling; cool off by idling, in refractory-lined tunnels, or at the surface.

children.title: Overheat throttle
children.description: Above 70 heat the drill slows to half speed, a warning before any damage.

children.title: Heat damage
children.description: At maximum heat the hull burns away steadily.

children.title: Lava pockets
children.description: Hidden pockets of lava in deeper bands of heat planets.

children.title: Flowing lava
children.description: Breach a pocket and lava pours down into open tunnels; refractory lining stops it.

children.title: Lava contact
children.description: Touching lava spikes heat and costs hull.

areas.title: Artefacts & Unique Items
areas.description: One-of-a-kind finds that change how you play, not just numbers.

children.title: Artefact cache
children.description: One sealed cache hides in every planet (band 3 on planet 1, band 2 after); a prompt shows when you're on it.

children.title: Pick one of three
children.description: Opening the cache offers three exclusive cards; 'Leave it' keeps the cache for later.

children.title: One artefact held
children.description: You keep one artefact for good; every other cache becomes an empty husk.

children.title: Artefacts
children.description: The three picks available now.

children.title: Ore Whisper
children.description: While undocked, ore within 16 m glows at its rim through up to 1 m of rock.

children.title: Breathing Room
children.description: Once per dock cycle, the first collapse warning on your tunnels is braced and refilled safely.

children.title: Assay Beacon
children.description: At the Sell bay, shallow-band ore sells at the mid-band price.

children.title: Planned artefact sets
children.description: More artefact picks in the campaign schedule.

children.title: Set I: Seismic ping, Second wind
children.description: Two new picks.

children.title: Set II: Ember valve, Overclock
children.description: Two new picks.

children.title: Set III: Thermal lance, Glide treads
children.description: Two new picks.

children.title: Set IV: Relay coil, Salvage magnet
children.description: Two new picks.

children.title: Set V: Grapple anchor, Core sense
children.description: Two new picks.

children.title: Archive cache
children.description: An exclusive story-fragment pick between the relic and hollow planets.

areas.title: Narrative & Onboarding
areas.description: Guild transmissions give the journey purpose; hints teach without a tutorial level.

children.title: Guild transmissions
children.description: Short text messages from the Guild that never pause play.

children.title: Opening transmission
children.description: 'Your rig stands on the pad, prospector': bring up ore, buy gear, dig to the core.

children.title: Core struck
children.description: Congratulates you on reaching the core and explains fragments buy passage onward.

children.title: Welcome to the second world
children.description: Warns that gravity pulls harder on planet 2.

children.title: Onboarding hints
children.description: Six one-time hints triggered by what you do.

children.title: Move hint
children.description: How to drive and use the thruster.

children.title: Drill hint
children.description: How to swivel the drill and bore.

children.title: Cargo hint
children.description: Ore fills the hold; go back and dock to sell.

children.title: Sell bay hint
children.description: The quick 'sell, repair and recharge' action.

children.title: Upgrade bay hint
children.description: Tells you when you can afford an upgrade and where to buy it.

children.title: Energy & tow hint
children.description: Energy is your clock; how to call the tow, and what a tow cost you.

children.title: Hint pacing
children.description: Hints are spaced at least 20 s apart, each shown once, remembered across reloads, and can be switched off.

children.title: No tutorial level
children.description: You learn in the real game, helped by a starter vein near the dock.

children.title: Planned story beats
children.description: Campaign story content scheduled for later planets.

children.title: Relic story planet
children.description: A story planet built around an ancient relic.

children.title: Finale key
children.description: A campaign cipher that opens the way to the finale.

children.title: Finale story planet
children.description: The campaign finale.

areas.title: HUD & UI
areas.description: Readable, colour-independent information while you dig.

children.title: Gauge cluster
children.description: Energy, hull and cargo as gauges with exact numbers, plus the cargo's sale value and any lining bill.

children.title: Heat gauge
children.description: On heat planets, a heat gauge that hatches and reads THROTTLED above its limit.

children.title: Depth & band readout
children.description: Depth below the surface (or altitude above it) and the current band.

children.title: Dock compass
children.description: An arrow and distance pointing home to the dock, plus tiles to the core's edge.

children.title: Time per tile
children.description: How long the rock in front of the drill will take, or 'needs a better tip'.

children.title: Status badges
children.description: Casing grade warning, guns mode with a low-steam badge, and charges carried with the plant key.

children.title: Warning banner
children.description: Low energy, a live charge fuse nearby, and the rig's state with the tow countdown.

children.title: Context prompts
children.description: Dock and artefact-cache prompts appear exactly when the action would work.

children.title: Threat markers
children.description: Edge-of-screen markers for enemies winding up, with the zone letter (F, S, R) they'd hit and a tremor sign for burrowers.

children.title: Big-number display
children.description: Very large money and prices shown in a compact, readable format.

children.title: Colour-independent design
children.description: Icons, letters and hatching back up every colour cue.

children.title: Icon set
children.description: Every gauge, status, readout, row, resource, button, card, plaque and setting has an icon; the frame shape says the kind (plate, gear, hex, triangle) and ore icons are generated from the ore look with their grade.

children.title: Combat status stack
children.description: Hull critical, collapse, live fuse, overheat, low energy and threat as triangle icons in that priority, at most three with a +N pip, pulsing by urgency (a thicker rim with flashes off); cargo full and the tow countdown shown beside them.

children.title: Keyboard menus
children.description: Every screen works with the keyboard: arrows move focus, Enter or Space confirms, Esc backs out.

areas.title: Audio
areas.description: Mechanical sound effects and layered music driven by what is happening in the game.

children.title: Sound effects
children.description: Sounds that change with what the rig is doing.

children.title: Drill voice
children.description: The drill strains lower on hard rock and sings higher in your own lining.

children.title: Engine & lift
children.description: The engine chugs faster with speed; the thruster hisses.

children.title: Ore pickup chime
children.description: A chime that climbs the scale with the ore's tier, so better ore sounds better.

children.title: Dock & upgrade clank
children.description: A heavy clank on docking and on buying upgrades.

children.title: Hit impact
children.description: Getting hit sounds sharp, with a shake and flash.

children.title: Casing hiss & pop
children.description: A hydraulic hiss as a ring is laid and a pop as the drill breaks through lining.

children.title: Collapse rumble & crash
children.description: A rising rumble during the warning, then a crash as the walls refill.

children.title: Wrecker scrape
children.description: A scrape when a tunnel wrecker breaches your route.

children.title: Charge blast
children.description: A crack and shake when your charge goes off.

children.title: Layered music
children.description: Four looping layers crossfade with where you are.

children.title: Platform layer
children.description: Plays while docked or near the hub.

children.title: Ambience layer
children.description: Underground; louder the deeper you go.

children.title: Tension layer
children.description: Deep bands or low energy.

children.title: Combat layer
children.description: Rises as enemies close in.

children.title: Per-planet tuning
children.description: Planets share the layers with their own tuning.

children.title: Music duck during artefact choice
children.description: Music dips while the artefact cards are open; the choice is never reported to the music, so this doesn't happen yet.

children.title: Stingers
children.description: Short musical cues for big moments.

children.title: Dock stinger
children.description: Plays on docking.

children.title: Core stinger
children.description: Plays when you break the first core tile.

children.title: Reveal stinger
children.description: Plays when a new platform facility bolts on.

children.title: New planet type stinger
children.description: Plays when you reach a new kind of planet.

children.title: Artefact stinger
children.description: Should play when the artefact choice opens; the music exists but has no trigger yet.

areas.title: Visuals & Art
areas.description: A lit 2.5D look of brass machinery in a dark, carved world, built to hold up at 4K.

children.title: Lit 2.5D rendering
children.description: Flat parts lit by the headlamp and a few lights, with bloom on glowing things.

children.title: Rotating camera
children.description: The camera rolls with the planet so 'toward the core' is always down the screen (or stays north-up if you prefer).

children.title: Zoom
children.description: Zoom between 8 and 20 m across the screen (default 12) with =, - and 0, or pinch and double tap on touch; the same framing at any resolution, capped on screens wider than 16:9.

children.title: 4K adaptive resolution
children.description: Rendering resolution adjusts to keep the frame rate while the UI stays sharp.

children.title: Fits every screen
children.description: One UI scale grows the HUD and screens with the screen and never shrinks them on a phone; screens wider than 64:27 are pillarboxed, and no art is upscaled on a 4K TV.

children.title: World look
children.description: How the ground and sky read.

children.title: Ground strata
children.description: Hand-made layered rock textures per band, wrapped around the planet and tinted per planet.

children.title: Carved edges
children.description: Tunnels carve smoothly with a lit edge.

children.title: Sky fade
children.description: The planet's sky at the surface fades to underground dark as you descend.

children.title: Lava & firebrick
children.description: Glowing lava tiles and firebrick refractory lining with glowing joints.

children.title: Effects
children.description: Short-lived visual feedback.

children.title: Drill sparks
children.description: Sparks fly where the drill bites, denser in lining.

children.title: Cement spray
children.description: A grey puff as each casing ring is laid.

children.title: Collapse cracks & dust
children.description: Branching cracks and falling dust before a cave-in.

children.title: Blast scorch
children.description: Scorch marks where charges blew.

children.title: Heat shimmer
children.description: The rig shimmers when it runs hot.

children.title: Screen shake & flash
children.description: Hits shake and flash the screen, capped and one big effect at a time.

children.title: Authored art
children.description: Blender-made parts and textures, plus vector icons.

children.title: Vehicle parts
children.description: The rig's parts in three visual tiers.

children.title: Platform hub & bays
children.description: The hub, both bays and their backdrops.

children.title: Creatures & cache
children.description: Crawler, burrower and the artefact cache.

children.title: Module art
children.description: Refinery bay, gun turret, charge rack and tunnel wrecker.

areas.title: Controls, Save & Settings
areas.description: Keyboard controls, the settings overlay and automatic saves.

children.title: Controls
children.description: A data-driven keyboard map.

children.title: Keyboard layout
children.description: WASD or arrows to drive, drill and lift; Space/E dock; Q quick service; R tow; G guns; B charge; = - 0 zoom; Esc settings.

children.title: Key rebinding
children.description: Rebind any action in settings, with conflicts refused and a reset to defaults.

children.title: Touch controls
children.description: On a phone or tablet: a floating stick on the left, a cluster of the buttons you can use now on the right, pinch to zoom; they hide when you type and come back on the next touch.

children.title: Gamepad & Steam Input
children.description: Controller support, cut from the slice; the control map is ready for it.

children.title: Settings
children.description: Presentation and accessibility options, kept apart from the save.

children.title: Camera mode
children.description: Camera rotating with the planet, or fixed north-up.

children.title: Screen shake / reduce motion
children.description: Turns off shake and part motion; bay shutters fade and installs are instant.

children.title: Flashes
children.description: Turns off screen flashes; warnings stay steady.

children.title: Show hints
children.description: Switch the onboarding hints on or off.

children.title: Music on/off & volume
children.description: Mute or set the music volume.

children.title: TV mode
children.description: Bigger text and controls for a TV across the room, kept inside a 5% overscan-safe border.

children.title: Left-handed touch & haptics
children.description: Mirror the touch controls for the left hand; a short buzz on drill contact and hull damage.

children.title: Saving
children.description: Checkpoint saves that you never have to think about.

children.title: Checkpoint autosave
children.description: The game saves at every dock, purchase, tow and travel.

children.title: Resume
children.description: Reload and you're back at the dock where you last saved.

children.title: Safe save handling
children.description: A save from an incompatible build is set aside, never overwritten, and a fresh run starts.

children.title: Multiple save slots
children.description: More than one slot; the slice has a single slot.

areas.title: Platforms & Multiplayer
areas.description: Where the game runs and who plays it.

children.title: Browser
children.description: Plays in a desktop browser and is published on GitHub Pages; saves go to browser storage.

children.title: Phones, tablets and TVs
children.description: Plays in landscape on phones and tablets with every screen reachable by touch; portrait shows a turn-your-device card. A screenshot matrix keeps desktop, phone, tablet and TV sizes checked.

children.title: Electron desktop build
children.description: A packaged desktop game folder per OS, ready for Steam depots, with saves, settings and logs in the user folder.

children.title: Steam integration
children.description: Overlay, cloud saves, achievements and SteamPipe uploads via steamworks.js; researched, not built.

children.title: Steam Deck verification
children.description: Steam Deck support after the slice.

children.title: Co-op multiplayer
children.description: 2-4 player co-op with shared world and platform but separate wallets and rigs. The game already runs through a co-op-ready authority; networking isn't built.

children.title: Performance & memory
children.description: Stays within frame and memory budgets over long sessions; budget work on ground carving and memory soaks is ongoing.

areas.title: Debug & Testing Tools
areas.description: Notable tools for testers and automated players (debug runs only).

children.title: Debug mode
children.description: Add ?debug to the URL (or --debug-api on desktop) to expose the debug API for tests and bots.

children.title: Scenarios
children.description: Start from a prepared situation with ?scenario= or a scenario file.

children.title: DEBUG RUN mark
children.description: A HUD mark once a debug command was used, so debug runs are never mistaken for real play.

children.title: Run logging
children.description: Every run writes an event log and summary to compare playthroughs.

children.title: Replays & golden runs
children.description: Seeded runs replay exactly and are checked against recorded golden runs.

children.title: Pacing bot & balance reports
children.description: An automated player plays the campaign and reports pace, guns, charges, refinery and heat balance.

children.title: Status dashboard
children.description: A public page with the issue tree, automated loop status and performance charts.

children.title: Session analysis & memory soak
children.description: Richer session logs, memory snapshots and a CI memory gate.

disagreements: **Schedule file is behind the code.** `docs/scaling/horizontal/stats.json` still marks slice-2 features as "building" or "planned" (fluid ground, casing, collapse, two bays, artefacts, music). All of them are in the code. The six campaign modules (refinery, guns, wrecker, charges, heat/lava, refractory lining) are marked shipped since #127.
**Plan text is out of date.** #90 still lists M1–M5 (#92–#96) as held or blocked, but all five are closed and merged.

**Music hooks for artefacts aren't connected.** The artefact stinger has music data but no trigger, and the music dip during the artefact choice is always off. Comments say both were waiting for S10 (#64), which has since shipped.

**Vision and code differ in scope.** design.md describes many ore families, repair and storage facilities, and powerups. The code has metal and crystal ores only. Repair is at the Upgrade bay (or the Sell bay's quick action). Powerups were deferred (#47); the slots and charges came back with the power-up core (#200), and the real power-ups are still to come.
**Heat came back.** The slice ruled out heat (#7, #2). It now exists only on the heat planets (8–16), added by the campaign plan (#96).

Built = in the code today; Partial = partly built; Planned = decided or scheduled in an issue but not built.
